# SEO-067: Bound the URL space that generated routes can produce

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

Routes whose parameters are open-ended - calendars, arbitrary date ranges, internal search queries, unbounded coordinate or id spaces - are limited to a finite enumerable set or excluded from crawling.

## Rationale

An unbounded parameter lets a crawler generate new addresses indefinitely, and each fetch consumes capacity that would otherwise go to pages that hold real content.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site",
    "has_router"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

For each dynamic segment, state the finite set of values the site intends to expose and reject the rest with 404. Where the space cannot be bounded, stop linking into it and disallow the path prefix instead of relying on the crawler to give up.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Request a generated route with an out-of-range parameter value and record whether it returns content, an error status, or another set of links deeper into the same space.
- Evidence: `ROUTE`, `HTTP_STATUS`, `ROBOTS_TXT`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
